name: SLAM and Mapping
text:
# SLAM and Mapping

Also called: 3DGS SLAM, Neural SLAM, Gaussian SLAM

## Overview
SLAM and Mapping in the context of [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) refers to the joint estimation of camera poses and the optimization of a 3D Gaussian scene representation from sequential or sparse sensor data. It solves the problem of building a consistent, high-fidelity, real-time renderable map in unknown environments, addressing challenges such as map drift, duplicate densification, and Gaussian degeneracy. It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Mapping Strategies](9321-mapping-strategies.md) by its focus on intra-scene consistency and pose estimation rather than cross-scene alignment, and from [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) Representation](12096-neural-radiance-field-nerf-representation.md) by using explicit, differentiable Gaussian primitives instead of implicit neural fields, enabling real-time rendering and direct gradient-based optimization of geometry and appearance [S1][S2, unofficial][S3].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves a coupled optimization loop where the scene representation $\mathcal{R}$ (a set of 3D Gaussians $\mathcal{G}$) and camera poses $\mathbf{T}_t$ are jointly or alternately optimized. Each Gaussian $i$ is defined by mean position $\mu_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$, covariance matrix $\Sigma_i \in \mathbb{R}^{3 \times 3}$ (parameterized by scale $\mathbf{s}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and rotation $\mathbf{R}_i \in SO(3)$), opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$, and color $c_i$.

The optimization objective minimizes a loss function $L$:
$$ L = L_{photo} + \lambda L_{depth} + L_{reg} $$
where $L_{photo} = || I_{rendered} - I_{captured} ||_1$ measures color difference, $L_{depth} = || D_{rendered} - D_{captured} ||_1$ measures depth difference (if available), and $L_{reg}$ includes [regularization terms](#1413-regularization-losses.md) such as scale isotropy to prevent degenerate Gaussians.

Key challenges include avoiding duplicate densification in well-reconstructed areas, mitigating map drift from accumulated pose errors, and preventing Gaussian degeneracy (overly anisotropic scales) through regularization.

## Subtopics

### [Mapping Strategies](9321-mapping-strategies.md)
[Mapping strategies](#9321-mapping-strategies.md) define the correspondence mechanism used to align pixels or features between two distinct 3D scenes or radiance fields, typically for tasks such as multi-scene editing, fusion, or transfer. Unlike standard SLAM mapping which aligns a current frame to a static map, these strategies address the alignment of two complete scene representations. They are distinguished from sibling methods like [Semantic-aware mapping](12053-semantic-aware-mapping.md) by their explicit focus on cross-scene pixel-to-pixel or feature-to-feature correspondence rather than intra-scene consistency.

### [3D Gaussian Splatting optimization](12052-3d-gaussian-splatting-optimization.md)
This family encompasses methods that optimize a scene representation composed of 3D Gaussians and camera poses to minimize photometric and geometric residuals between rendered views and captured sensor data. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Mapping Strategies](9321-mapping-strategies.md) and [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) Representation](12096-neural-radiance-field-nerf-representation.md) by using explicit, differentiable Gaussian primitives rather than implicit neural fields or voxel grids, allowing for real-time rendering and direct gradient-based optimization of geometry and appearance.

### [Semantic-aware mapping](12053-semantic-aware-mapping.md)

### [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) Representation](12096-neural-radiance-field-nerf-representation.md)
[Neural Radiance Fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) ([NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md)) represent a 3D scene as a continuous volumetric function parameterized by a multi-layer perceptron (MLP), enabling the synthesis of novel views from a sparse set of input images by solving the [volume rendering integral](#8682-volume-rendering-integral.md). Unlike explicit representations such as [3D Gaussian Splatting](12052-3d-gaussian-splatting-optimization.md) which store millions of discrete blobs, NeRF stores the scene implicitly within a neural network, allowing for high-fidelity, view-dependent appearance modeling with significantly lower memory footprint, albeit at the cost of slower rendering and training times.

#### CG-SLAM
CG-SLAM introduces an uncertainty map into the training process based on the rendered depth, which greatly improves the reconstruction quality [S1].

#### Combined ORB-SLAM + 3DGS
This approach combines an existing frame-based tracking system (ORB-SLAM) with 3DGS mapping. ORB-SLAM recovers poses, and 3DGS is trained with poses and sensor depth of keyframes, equivalent to offline [splatting](#23-splatting.md) [S2, unofficial]. On EuRoC Machine Hall (Stereo Depth), the ATE [RMSE](#10453-depth-accuracy-metrics.md) (m) for ORB-SLAM3 is 0.052, while the combined approach yields 3.190. Point-SLAM fails on all sequences [S2, unofficial]. While ORB-SLAM achieves the best ATE, the combined approach shows no significant difference in rendering metrics compared to unified 3DGS SLAM. The unified approach is preferred for exploring 3DGS throughout the entire algorithm [S2, unofficial].

#### CP-SLAM
CP-SLAM is a neural point-based hybrid neural field SLAM system enabling multi-agent cooperative localization and mapping with loop closure [S3]. It uses a keyframe-associated [neural point representation](#7266-neural-points.md) inspired by PointNeRF, allowing per-point features to be adjusted during pose graph optimization [S3]. It employs a two-stage distributed-to-centralized training scheme: initial decoders are trained separately for each agent, then fused and fine-tuned jointly [S3]. It integrates odometry, loop detection, sub-map fusion, and global refinement into a unified framework [S3].

#### MNE-SLAM
MNE-SLAM is the first fully distributed multi-agent neural SLAM framework enabling accurate collaborative mapping and robust camera tracking without centralized training or raw data exchange [S3]. It uses a triplane+MLP hybrid neural field representation as a mapping module [S3]. It introduces an intra-to-inter loop closure strategy to reduce pose drift and align submaps across agents through peer-to-peer feature sharing and global consistency loss [S3].

#### HERO-SLAM
HERO-SLAM is a SLAM method employing a novel multiscale patch-based loss that aligns feature points, maps, and RGB-D pixels through warpings [S3]. It uses an INGP-like multiresolution hybrid feature grid+MLP representation for neural [SDF](#1466-signed-distance-fields-sdf.md) learning [S3].

#### PIN-SLAM
PIN-SLAM is a globally consistent SLAM system using a point-based implicit neural (PIN) representation [S3]. It replaces grid structures with neural feature points, offering spatial flexibility and elastic correction during loop closure [S3]. Mapping alternates with odometry [S3]. The mapping step is based on a hybrid neural SDF representation with explicit neural points and implicit MLP decoders [S3]. Odometry is performed correspondence-free via second-order scan-to-map optimization [S3]. A sliding window replay buffer ensures stable incremental updates [S3]. Loop closures trigger pose graph optimization and elastic deformation of neural points, enabling consistent large-scale mapping [S3].

#### Active 3D Reconstruction Algorithm
This algorithm performs active 3D reconstruction using a radiance field.
1.  **Initialization:** Initialize 3D bounding box, uniformly sample goal-state candidates $S_g$ from view space, initialize DVGO coarse model $M^{(c)}$ and agent state $s_0$, append initial image to database $\{I\}$ [S4, unofficial].
2.  **Global Policy:** Select next-best-view $s^*_g$ from goal candidates $S_g$ using criterion: $s^*_g = \arg \min_{s_g \in S_g} (\lambda_{cp} l_{cp}(x_{s_g}) - \lambda_{ig} E_s(s_g))$, where $x_{s_g}$ is 3D location of $s_g$ [S4, unofficial].
3.  **Local Policy:** Execute planning optimization to obtain optimized trajectory $S^*$ and local next-best view $s^*$ [S4, unofficial].
4.  **Action:** Move agent to $s^*$ [S4, unofficial].
5.  **Observation:** Obtain new image observation $I_t$ [S4, unofficial].
6.  **Update Database:** Add new observation to database $\{I\}_{i=0}^{t+1}$ [S4, unofficial].
7.  **Mapping Optimization:** Optimize DVGO model $M_t$ to $M_{t+1}$ by sampling pixels from database, including synchronizing entropy volume $V(E,c)$ [S4, unofficial].
8.  **Stop Check:** Stop if (1) change in entropy volume is below threshold, or (2) maximum information gain of feasible goal candidates is below threshold [S4, unofficial].
9.  **Fine Stage:** After exploration, initialize DVGO fine model $M^{(f)}$ with trained coarse model $M_T^{(c)}$. Perform stochastic training by sampling pixels from database $\{I\}_{i=0}^T$ for $N$ iterations, optimizing every $m$ iterations [S4, unofficial].

## Background
The integration of SLAM with 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) leverages the explicit geometry representation provided by 3DGS, which enables flexible reprojection to alleviate misalignment between different viewpoints, leading to better reconstruction compared to NeRF-based methods [S1]. The real-time rendering feature of 3DGS also makes neural-based SLAM methods more applicable for robotics tasks such as relocalization, navigation, 6D pose estimation, multi-sensor calibration, and manipulation [S1]. Early works like CG-SLAM improved reconstruction quality by introducing uncertainty maps based on rendered depth [S1]. Combined approaches with classical SLAM systems like ORB-SLAM demonstrated that while classical methods may achieve lower ATE, unified 3DGS-based methods offer competitive rendering metrics and better integration with the Gaussian representation [S2, unofficial]. Hybrid neural field approaches (e.g., CP-SLAM, PIN-SLAM, HERO-SLAM) have also been developed to address challenges in multi-agent scenarios, loop closure, and semantic consistency, often using point-based or grid+MLP representations [S3]. Active reconstruction algorithms using radiance fields (e.g., ActiveRMAP) utilize information gain and entropy volume to guide camera motion for efficient mapping [S4, unofficial].
